hero.title: Let the Agent build your data migration pipelines
hero.sub: Design, run, schedule and govern pipelines, all on this computer

workspace.title: Welcome to Otter ETL agent
workspace.subtitle: Pick a folder to store your workspace
workspace.lead: Otter ETL agent keeps your pipelines, saved connections, contexts, routines, and documentation in a regular folder on disk. Everything is plain JSON so it plays nicely with version control.
workspace.existingDesc: If you already have an Otter ETL agent workspace, point at the same folder and your saved state loads automatically.
workspace.newTitle: Or choose a new empty folder
workspace.newDesc: Otter ETL agent creates its workspace files (duckle.json, repository.json) on first save. Use any folder - a fresh one, your Documents folder, anywhere.
workspace.noFolder: No folder selected. Pick a directory where Otter ETL agent can store pipelines, connections, and routines.

engine.title: Workspace initialisation
engine.subtitle: First-run setup - Otter ETL agent stays a tiny download and fetches the DuckDB engine and dbt Fusion now. Sample pipelines and data are added to a new workspace so you have something to run right away.
engine.required: DuckDB is required to run pipelines.
engine.dbtDesc: Fast dbt engine for the dbt transform node. Installs alongside DuckDB; the dbt-core fallback is fetched automatically if Fusion is unavailable.
engine.dbtRetry: {{error}} - you can retry, or install it later when you use a dbt node.

wizard.chooseTitle: How are you using Otter ETL agent?
wizard.chooseSub: You can change this later. Nothing here is permanent.
wizard.localSub: Draw pipelines and run them here. No server, nothing to set up.
wizard.teamSub: Author here and deploy to a server you own, where pipelines run on a schedule.
wizard.whereSub: Otter ETL agent is one binary, so this only changes the command you run. You own the machine either way.
wizard.standupCustom: Start an Otter ETL agent server
wizard.bindNote: It binds to 0.0.0.0 rather than 127.0.0.1 on purpose. A server that only answers on loopback counts as already yours and cannot be claimed from here.
wizard.addressSub: The address of a machine running duckle-runner serve.
wizard.claimSub: Put your name in and it becomes yours. You decide who else gets in, and what they can do.
wizard.codeNote: The server printed a setup code when it started. Read it from the terminal it runs in, or from docker logs. Seeing that output is what proves you own the server rather than merely being able to reach it. The code is new every restart and is never stored.
wizard.keyNote: Its key is saved here, encrypted, and never shown again. That is the whole of what this machine keeps.
wizard.keyTitle: This server is already set up
wizard.keySub: Ask an administrator for a key. In the console that is People, then Create key.
wizard.doneSub: Build a pipeline here, then deploy it to {{name}}. Its schedule arrives switched off, so nothing starts running until you say so.
wizard.adminToken: This is your administrator sign-in for {{url}}. It is shown once and cannot be recovered, so keep it somewhere safe.
wizard.tokenNote: Otter ETL agent already saved its own encrypted copy for deploying, so you only need this one to open the console in a browser.

custom.name: Custom
custom.blurb: A machine you run yourself, including this one
custom.step1: Save the runner (below). It comes out of this app, so there is nothing to download.
custom.step2: Paste the command it gives you into a terminal.
custom.step3: Wait for the line that says NOT SET UP, then come back here.

aws.blurb: EC2, ECS on Fargate, or EKS
aws.step1: Launch an EC2 instance with Docker, and open port 8080 to yourself only.
aws.step2: Run the container, giving it a folder for the workspace.
aws.step3: Wait for the line that says NOT SET UP.

gcp.blurb: Compute Engine, Cloud Run, or GKE
gcp.runsOn: Compute Engine is the straightforward one
gcp.step1: Create an instance from the container image.
gcp.step2: Allow yourself through the firewall on port 8080.
gcp.step3: Wait for the line that says NOT SET UP.

azure.blurb: Virtual Machine, Container Apps, or AKS
azure.runsOn: A VM is the straightforward one
azure.step1: Create a Linux VM with Docker, and restrict inbound to yourself.
azure.step2: Run the container, giving it a folder for the workspace.
azure.step3: Wait for the line that says NOT SET UP.
